title: XEX1 binary preview frame — DECODED-body descriptor (sketch)
description: SKETCH, with a caveat that is itself a headline finding. The real XEX1 frame is NOT JSON: it is the 4-byte magic "XEX1" followed by a msgpack body, pushed as a WebSocket BINARY frame via emit_binary. JSON Schema describes JSON documents, so it CANNOT describe: (a) the magic-prefix framing, (b) the msgpack encoding/type tags (fixmap vs map16, bin8/16/32), or (c) the raw JPEG bytes in each image. This schema describes only the msgpack body's LOGICAL structure AFTER decoding to a JSON-shaped object, and models the opaque JPEG payload as a placeholder string. Two real invariants live entirely OUTSIDE this schema and would need a separate binary-IDL/format tool: the fixmap<=15-key cap (expose.cpp emits fixmap only) and the msgpack type coverage the three hand-rolled codecs must agree on. See the binary-frame finding in the writeup: JSON Schema is the wrong tool for XEX1.

jpeg.description: OPAQUE. On the wire this is msgpack `bin` (raw JPEG bytes), un-representable in JSON; modelled here as a base64/placeholder string ONLY so the decoded-body descriptor is expressible. A binary IDL would type this as bytes with a length; JSON Schema cannot.

seq.description: = run_id ($seq). int64 on the wire — a JSON-number model would lose precision above 2^53; a real binary format keeps it a fixed-width int. Another reason JSON Schema under-serves the binary path.

json.description: Record scalars serialized to a JSON STRING (the decoder does one JSON.parse); key order = insertion/display order.
